note: Analyst Shark, security angle. Findings limited to issues that survive the inclusion test (North Star–traceable). Changelog was opaque (N× “Applied a search/replace patch”) and was not treated as evidence of fix.

findings.topic: preview path sandbox and magic-byte guard missing
findings.criterion: without … a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: W18’s “binary guard” is only content-type → named unsupported-preview. There is no path sandbox (resolve under an allowed root; refuse `..`, absolute escape, symlink/junction by name) and no magic-byte / content sniff before render. A path that escapes the intended tree, or a file whose declared type is wrong, can still stream raw bytes into a text view — exactly the North Star violation. The binary-guard test only asserts absence of `PK\x03\x04` on happy-path fixtures; it never forces refusal on path escape or type/magic mismatch. Until escape-attempt + magic-byte refusal are deliverables with acceptance criteria, “no raw binary as text” is unenforced prose.

findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.message: The release guard is specified only as a “branch and channel check.” That does not prove v1.2-only modules (cost_state migration, named_state, dead_control, Doctor engines, new surface handlers) are excluded from v1.1.x packaging, installers, shared artifact channels, or cherry-picks. Collaborators on v1.1.x can still receive this effort’s code/artifacts if packaging is ungoverned. Branch name alone is not “nothing ships.” Require an artifact/package allowlist (or explicit exclude list of this build’s new paths) plus a failing test that a simulated v1.1.x package build cannot include those paths.

findings.topic: runtime path containment absent for open/preview/diagnose
findings.section: W1 containment vs W10 / W14 / W18; property gates containment
findings.criterion: open, run … real Anchor work without a dead control / mislabelled empty; preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: Escape-attempt coverage exists only for Foreman write containment under `planning/sleep-2026-07-28/stage2/`. Open, run workspace resolution, file preview, and Doctor path/version reads have zero escape-attempt acceptance criteria. Property-gate “containment” fires only “where containment is claimed,” and runtime surfaces never claim it — so the gate never fires. A control that opens or previews a path outside the intended workspace can present foreign content as legitimate work, mislabel empty/unknown relative to the wrong root, or dump raw binary. That is a security-shaped honesty failure on the North Star’s open/run/preview verbs, not a nice-to-have hardening add-on. Bind path sandbox + escape refusal into W10 and W18 (and Doctor live path reads in W14) with the same refusal-by-name pattern W1 already uses for build writes.

findings.section: Wave 2 exit_register; Wave 1 task triple; Wave 5 freeze; Wave 22 S1
findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: “Signature validator,” “John’s dated confirmation line,” and freeze/exit stamps are schema fields with no host-bound or out-of-band identity check. `attestation.py` rejects sub-agent EXECUTION-LOG attestations, but nothing equivalent binds John-signed exit rows, the task triple, or the wave-list freeze. A wave or sub-agent can write a plausible confirmation string and green-path exits, freeze, and S1 prerequisites. That reopens silent structural claims of North Star readiness — the exact failure S1 exists to prevent. Specify a non-forgeable confirmation mechanism (host-only prompt, separate signed file John produces outside the agent write path, or equivalent) and a test that agent-written “John” lines are rejected.

findings.criterion: session attach … without … a dead control; fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty)
findings.message: Attach honesty covers timeout vs unknown_session, single error print, and Retry/cannot-retry. It never binds the attach request to a verified session identity (stable session id, process handle, owner, generation token). A wrong-session attach that returns success with another session’s stream is neither timeout nor unknown — it is a silent wrong attach, which is a security and honesty failure under “session attach” in the North Star. Add a cannot-attach / identity-mismatch named state, require handle verification before success, and an induced-fault test where a mismatched id cannot render as a successful attach.

findings.topic: diagnose live readings without secret redaction
findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose … every surface that claims health … or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: W14 bans fixed seed strings and requires findings to quote live readings (paths, versions, counts). It has no redaction or refusal path when a live reading contains credentials, tokens, or API keys. A diagnose that “works” by painting secrets into the Doctor tile is a confident wrong health/diagnose surface — parallel to raw-binary preview on the file surface. Require a secret-pattern refusal (or redacted-reading named state) with a test that injects a key-shaped reading and asserts it never appears in rendered HTML, and that the surface shows a named cannot_show_reading / redacted state instead of success-with-secret.

findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; surfaces fail with named states rather than silent wrong answers
findings.message: `fault_inject.py` can induce timeout, missing capability, empty result, unmeasured cost, and stale telemetry. No deliverable requires test-only enforcement (import guard, env flag, refuse outside pytest/CI). If production handlers can call it, live surfaces can be forced into fabricated named states — honesty inverted. Add a hard production refuse path and a test that production-mode import/invoke raises and cannot alter rendered state.

findings.topic: probe transcripts may ship secrets to collaborators
findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.message: Capability probes capture live transcripts under the shared planning tree, replayed many times, with a 14-day staleness rule on verdicts but no redaction, retention bound, or scrub gate on transcript bodies. Live v1.2 environment output (paths, session ids, cost rows, engine errors) can land in repo-tracked artifacts that collaborators receive. Release_guard’s branch/channel check does not scrub or quarantine these. Require secret scrub + explicit non-shipping classification for `artifacts/transcripts/` (or store outside the collaborator-facing tree) with a release-guard test that fails if raw transcript material is present in a v1.1.x-publishable package set.

findings.criterion: open, run … real Anchor work without meeting a dead control
findings.message: Run enumerates CannotRun reasons (no target, engine unavailable, prior run in flight, capability absent) but never constrains how project/target strings reach the engine process. Unsanitized argv/shell construction lets a crafted project path or target name become command injection — a successful-looking Run that is not “real Anchor work.” That is a security-shaped dead/wrong control. Enumerate injection/escape as CannotRun (or refuse) reasons, ban shell=True-style invocation in acceptance tests, and add a fixture that dangerous metacharacters in a target cannot spawn unintended commands and must render a named cannot-run state.

findings.criterion: preview that dumps raw binary; open … real Anchor work
findings.message: Unsupported types get “named unsupported-preview + download affordance,” but download is not bound to the same path sandbox as preview. A download that follows an escaped path exfiltrates arbitrary files while the UI claims a safe named state. Extend the W18 path sandbox to the download action with an escape-attempt test; otherwise the named state is honesty theater around a second exfil channel.

findings.topic: property gates omit security while plan asserts integrity controls
findings.message: The plan asserts signature validation, host-computed attestation, release isolation, and path refusal in places, but the emitted property-gate checklist only lists honesty, idempotence, boundedness, containment. There is no security/integrity gate (authz of confirmations, secret redaction, package quarantine). Under the plan’s own rule this is not a property-named-but-unenforced BLOCKER unless security is named as a property. Recorded for synthesis only; do not keep the loop open on this alone.
